answer: An agent economy can price identity through a mirrored endorsement graph. Two existing agents must co-sign a newcomer, each escrowing stake and publishing a cipher commitment to a shared task transcript neither can forge alone. The registry then publishes a shuffled mirror of the graph's adjacency, hiding names but keeping edge weights; auditors scan it for marble-smooth cliques, meaning rings whose members only endorse one another. A ring's bonded stake is slashed, so a thousand fake agents cost a thousand real bonds plus two colluding sponsors apiece.
